close_reason: Implemented bidirectional AVA matching in names_match (a⊆b AND b⊆a). This correctly rejects {CN=Alice,CN=Alice} vs {CN=Bob,CN=Alice} where old .any() gave a false positive. O(n²) on AVA count; n≤5 in practice; no heap needed. All 28 pkix-path unit tests pass.
description: pkix-path/src/lib.rs names_match(): the .any() loop checks that every AVA in a_rdn has a matching AVA in b_rdn, but it allows the same b_rdn entry to satisfy multiple a_rdn entries. Concrete trigger: a_rdn={CN=Alice, CN=Alice} (duplicate CN) with b_rdn={CN=Bob, CN=Alice} (len=2, count check passes). For the first a_ava=CN=Alice, .any() finds CN=Alice in b_rdn → true. For the second a_ava=CN=Alice, .any() again finds CN=Alice in b_rdn → true. Result: the two different RDNs are incorrectly considered equal. This requires an adversarially crafted cert with a duplicate OID in one RDN. While RFC 5280 §5.1.2.4 says SHOULD NOT, the library processes untrusted input. A name collision could allow a forged intermediate cert's subject to match a trust anchor's name. Fix: use bijective (matched-pair) set comparison for RDN AVAs.
title: names_match not bijective for RDNs with duplicate-OID AVAs
